Catalan

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Latin pressa.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (Central, Balearic) [ˈpɾe.sə]
  • IPA(key): (Valencia) [ˈpɾe.sa]
  • Audio (Barcelona):(file)

Noun

[edit]

pressa f (plural presses)

  1. hurry, haste
    no corre pressa ― there is no hurry

Derived terms

[edit]
  • apressar
  • de pressa

Further reading

[edit]
  • “pressa”, in Diccionari de la llengua catalana [Dictionary of the Catalan Language] (in Catalan), second edition, Institute of Catalan Studies [Catalan: Institut d'Estudis Catalans], April 2007

Finnish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Clipping of presidentti (“president”) +‎ -sa.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈpresːɑ/, [ˈpre̞s̠ːɑ̝]
  • Rhymes: -esːɑ
  • Syllabification(key): pres‧sa
  • Hyphenation(key): pres‧sa

Noun

[edit]

pressa (informal)

  1. prez (president)

Icelandic

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈpʰrɛsːa/
  • Rhymes: -ɛsːa

Etymology 1

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

pressa f (genitive singular pressu, nominative plural pressur)

  1. press (tool)
  2. printing press
    Synonym: prentvél
  3. (uncountable, usually with definite article) press (printed media)
Declension
[edit]
Declension of pressa (feminine)
singular plural
indefinite definite indefinite definite
nominative pressa pressan pressur pressurnar
accusative pressu pressuna pressur pressurnar
dative pressu pressunni pressum pressunum
genitive pressu pressunnar pressa pressanna

Etymology 2

[edit]

Verb

[edit]

pressa (weak verb, third-person singular past indicative pressaði, supine pressað)

  1. to press, to squeeze [with accusative]
    Synonym: fergja
  2. to press, to iron [with accusative]
    Synonym: strauja

Italian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈprɛs.sa/
  • Rhymes: -ɛssa
  • Hyphenation: près‧sa

Etymology 1

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

pressa f (plural presse)

  1. press
  2. crowd, press
Related terms
[edit]
  • pressare
  • torchio

Etymology 2

[edit]

See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

Verb

[edit]

pressa

  1. inflection of pressare:
    1. third-person singular present
    2. second-person singular imperative

Anagrams

[edit]
  • sparse, spersa

Latin

[edit]

Participle

[edit]

pressa

  1. inflection of pressus:
    1. nominative/vocative feminine singular
    2. nominative/accusative/vocative neuter plural

Participle

[edit]

pressā

  1. ablative feminine singular of pressus

References

[edit]
  • "pressa", in Charles du Fresne du Cange, Glossarium Mediæ et Infimæ Latinitatis (augmented edition with additions by D. P. Carpenterius, Adelungius and others, edited by Léopold Favre, 1883–1887)
  • “pressa”, in Gaffiot, Félix (1934), Dictionnaire illustré latin-français, Hachette.
  • pressa in Ramminger, Johann (16 July 2016 (last accessed)), Neulateinische Wortliste: Ein Wörterbuch des Lateinischen von Petrarca bis 1700‎[2], pre-publication website, 2005-2016

Neapolitan

From Latin pressus.

Pronunciation

  • IPA(key): /pressɐ/

Noun

[edit]

pressa

  1. (uncountable) hurry

Norwegian Bokmål

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • pressen (of presse (noun))
  • pressene (of press (noun))

Noun

[edit]

pressa m or f

  1. definite feminine singular of presse

Noun

[edit]

pressa n

Verb

pressa

    1. simple past
    2. past participle

Norwegian Nynorsk

[edit]

pressa f

pressa n

Portuguese

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈpɾɛ.sɐ/
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈpɾɛ.sɐ/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈpɾɛ.sa/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈpɾɛ.sɐ/

  • Audio (Portugal (Porto)):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɛsɐ
  • Hyphenation: pres‧sa

Etymology 1

[edit]

Inherited from Latin pressam.

Noun

[edit]

pressa f (plural pressas)

  1. hurry; rush; haste
    Não tenho nenhuma pressa. ― I'm not in a hurry.

Etymology 2

[edit]

Contraction

[edit]

pressa

  1. (nonstandard, informal) contraction of pra +‎ essa: feminine singular of presse

Further reading

[edit]
  • “pressa”, in Dicionário Aulete Digital (in Portuguese), Rio de Janeiro: Lexikon Editora Digital, 2008–2026
  • “pressa”, in Dicionário Priberam da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Lisbon: Priberam, 2008–2026
